content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a comprehensive rationale and strategy for the global elimination of congenital syphilis. This document outlines the necessary actions to achieve this goal and is accessible online. 2. WHO has developed methods for the surveillance and monitoring of congenital syphilis within existing health systems. These methods are detailed in a publication available on their website. 3. A data quality assurance tool for program-level indicators has been created by MEASURE Evaluation, based in Chapel Hill. This tool is designed to enhance the accuracy and reliability of health data and is available for download. 4. Guidelines for on-site data verification (OSDV) and rapid service quality assessment (RSQA) have been established to ensure the quality of health services. These guidelines are accessible online. 5. WHO has issued guidelines for conducting HIV surveillance using routine program data. These guidelines provide a framework for monitoring HIV trends and are available for reference. 6. Data exchange standards for electronic medical records have been developed to facilitate the integration and interoperability of health information systems. These standards are outlined in a document available online. 7. WHO and the Health Metrics Network have created a framework and standards for country health information systems. This document provides guidance on improving health data systems and is accessible online. 8. A joint inter-ministerial policy dialogue on eHealth standardization and the second WHO forum on eHealth standardization and interoperability have been conducted. The outcomes of these events are documented and available online. 9. WHO has published guidelines on protecting the confidentiality and security of HIV information. These guidelines were developed following a workshop held in Geneva and are available for download. 10. WHO has developed three interlinked patient monitoring systems for HIV care/ART, maternal and child health (MCH)/prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), and TB/HIV. These systems include a standardized minimum data set and illustrative tools, which are accessible online. 11. WHO has provided a framework for evaluating national surveillance systems. This framework is detailed in a publication available on their website. 12. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) has developed data quality assurance tools to support monitoring and evaluation systems. These tools are available for download from the MEASURE Evaluation website. 13. WHO has created a data quality report card to assess the quality of health data. This tool is accessible online. 14. Standards and tools for data quality assurance in PMTCT programs have been developed by WHO's Interagency Task Team on the Prevention and Treatment of HIV Infection in Pregnant Women. These resources are forthcoming. 15. WHO has published a handbook on monitoring the building blocks of health systems. This handbook includes indicators and measurement strategies and is available for download. 16. A comprehensive approach for scaling up HIV rapid testing in developing countries has been outlined by experts. This approach emphasizes the implementation of quality assurance measures and is detailed in a publication. 17. WHO has issued guidelines for conducting HIV surveillance using routine program data. These guidelines are accessible online. 18. WHO has published a report on the operational characteristics of HIV assays, including rapid diagnostic tests for detecting HIV-1/2 antibodies. This report is available for download. 19. Consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services have been developed by WHO. These guidelines provide recommendations for implementing HIV testing services and are accessible online. 20. The US Department of Health and Human Services has issued guidelines for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of HIV rapid testing. These guidelines apply a quality system approach and are available for download. 21. USAID has developed the Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) program, which provides data on population and health trends. Information about this program is available online. 22. Research has been conducted to measure the impact of HIV on fertility in Africa. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 23. A study has examined the impact of HIV status and perceived status on fertility desires in rural Malawi. The results are published in a peer-reviewed journal and available online. 24. Research has investigated the incidence of pregnancy after initiating antiretroviral therapy and associated factors in eight West African countries. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 25. The United Nations Joint Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) has developed a global plan to eliminate new HIV infections among children by 2015 and keep their mothers alive. This plan is documented and available for download. 26. A study has explored HIV prevalence patterns by age and sex across 19 countries. The findings are published in an analytical report and accessible online. 27. UNAIDS has published a report on the global AIDS epidemic in 2013. This report provides insights into the state of the epidemic and is available for download. 28. Research has analyzed the time from HIV seroconversion to death in lowand middle-income countries before the advent of highly active antiretroviral therapy. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 29. A study has examined trends in HIV prevalence and sexual behavior among young people aged 15-24 in countries most affected by HIV. The results are published in a peer-reviewed journal and available online. 30. Research has investigated trends in HIV prevalence among young people in generalized epidemics and their implications for monitoring the HIV epidemic. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 31. A study has projected the time course and magnitude of the AIDS epidemic among older children and adolescents in Southern Africa. The results are published in a peer-reviewed journal and available online. 32. Research has provided evidence of increasing adolescent HIV prevalence in Eastern Zimbabwe, suggesting the presence of long-term survivors of mother-to-child transmission. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 33. A pooled analysis of individual data from sub-Saharan Africa has examined the net survival of perinatally and postnatally HIV-infected children. The results are published in a peer-reviewed journal and available online. 34. WHO has issued guidance for HIV testing and counseling and care for adolescents living with HIV. These recommendations are designed for a public health approach and are accessible online. 35. WHO has published guidelines for using HIV testing technologies in surveillance. These guidelines cover selection, evaluation, and implementation and are available for download. 36. The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine has developed a rapid syphilis test toolkit. This guide provides instructions for planning, management, and implementation and is accessible online. 37. WHO has issued guidelines for conducting HIV surveillance using routine program data. These guidelines are accessible online. 38. A study has reviewed public health surveillance in the United States. The findings are published in a peer-reviewed journal and accessible online. 39. A publication has provided guidance on effectively communicating public health data to the public, policymakers, and the press. This resource is available from Oxford University Press.
